title: Knots across time are minimal decisive sets
claim: A deterministic local dynamics written as its space-time law (allowed states: the trajectories), read with K1-K3. (1) The knots made of one cell's value after T steps and first-row cells are exactly S + {y} for the minimally decisive sets S of the T-step map (some setting of S fixes it, no proper subset is decisive) with at least two cells; a decisive single cell gives a tie. (2) A nonconstant Boolean function has no such knot exactly when it is a single conjunction or a single disjunction of literals: a process knows its past only pairwise exactly there. (3) For a linear rule with polynomial p the only two-time knot at lag T is the support of p^T plus the cell, with |supp p| + 1 places at every lag 2^k (Frobenius) and 2^popcount(T) + 1 for rule 60 (Lucas); intermediate rows give smaller knots, 2 + w(T) places in rule 102's light cone for T <= 6 (Ledrappier's law, w the non-adjacent-form weight). (4) In Conway's Life the knots joining a cell's next value to the present are the 70 sets of four neighbours; the cell's own present value is in none.
failure_conditions: A knot of a T-step map's graph that is not a minimally decisive set plus the output, or the converse.
A nonconstant function with no knot in its graph that is not a single AND or OR of literals, or a term or clause with a knot.
A linear rule with more than one two-time knot at some lag.
foundation_claim_scope: Theorems 1-3 by proof; Proposition 4 by exhaustion over nine cells. Computed: all 88 elementary rules at T = 1, 2 and 300 random functions of 5 and 6 inputs against the generic enumerator; every nonconstant function of up to 4 inputs, all terms and clauses of 5 and 300 random 5-input functions; six linear and affine rules to T = 6 and Lucas to T = 32; rule 102's light cone to T = 6; Life's step.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-08.
validation.status: by hand, with the finite claims checked by computation with controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: implicants and certificates of Boolean functions (Buhrman and de Wolf 2002), Lucas's theorem and Frobenius for linear automata, Ledrappier's shift and its Frobenius triangles are classical; new as far as found is the reading under K1-K3: a process's knots across time are the minimal decisive sets of its future values, pairwise memory is exactly the single ANDs and ORs, and linear processes keep a fixed-size knot with their past at every power of two.
